temas.concepto: Cuando le diste tanto a algo que irte se siente como tirarte vos mismo a la basura — y te quedás, no por amor, sino porque no bancás soltar la cuenta.
temas.voz: Voz masculina, grave y susurrada en los versos, cruda y abierta en el estribillo, casi hablada en el bridge
temas.caption: Dark pop, pitched 808 bass, sparse detuned piano, vinyl crackle, slow trap hi-hats, ambient pads, melancholic, introspective, 82 BPM. Male voice, low breathy verses, raw open chorus, half-whispered bridge.
temas.letra:
[intro]
Mm-mm... mm-mm...

[verse]
Moved my books across the bridge, January rain
Taped the boxes with both names — your writing, then my strain
I learned to sleep along the left, I learned to like the cold
Knew your coffee order by the time I was nineteen years old
The savings bled through March and I didn't say a word
I pawned the chain my mother left — you never even heard
Six years of rent in someone else's town, someone else's street
I put down roots in borrowed ground before I felt the heat

[pre-chorus]
And now you're asking why I stay
As if the door still opens the same way

[chorus]
Too far in to find the door
Too far in to know who I was before
Every box I moved still pins me to this floor
I'm too far in — what was it for?

[verse]
The lease came up in autumn, felt it tighten in my chest
A slant of light across the room — I turned and faced the rest
Your jacket on the kitchen chair like it had always hung
The coffee pot still set for two, the morning barely strung
I typed a one-way ticket in the browser late at night
The price so low it mocked me, every digit burning bright
I closed the tab and washed the cups and ironed all your shirts
I've stitched myself into this seam too tight to feel it hurts

[pre-chorus]
And still you're asking why I stay
As if I'd recognize myself away

[chorus]
Too far in to find the door
Too far in to know who I was before
Every box I moved still pins me to this floor
I'm too far in — what was it for?

[bridge]
What if this was never love — just math I couldn't undo?
A ledger full of everything I ever gave to you
The penny jar so full by now it cannot leave the shelf
I'd have to break the glass to go — the shards would take what's left

[chorus]
Too far in to find the door
Too far in to know who I was before
I could lift the boxes, I could leave this floor
But I'm too far in — I always need one more

[outro]
One more... one more...

temas.concepto: Se aferra a la nostalgia de una ciudad que nunca existió, una promesa de pertenencia que solo se encuentra en la memoria y la adicción.
temas.voz: dúo: él, voz grave con flow entrecortado; ella, susurros angelicales y resonantes
temas.captionInstrumental: dark trap, cinematic trap, gliding 808 bass, crisp trap hi-hats with triplets, haunting bells, granular textures, spacious reverb, melancholic pads, slow tempo.
temas.captionVoces: Male rapper: deep, textured voice, double-time flow. Female voice: breathy, ethereal, layered harmonies, haunting ad-libs.
temas.beat: The call transforms into a backwards echo during the bridge, symbolizing the distorted memories of a lost place.

historia.quien: The narrator is a young man, mid-twenties, living in a rapidly gentrifying industrial district of Buenos Aires, Argentina, circa 2010. He's a former street artist, now working a dead-end job in a warehouse, feeling disconnected and haunted by the city’s fading working-class identity.
historia.verso1: The verse opens with the narrator standing on a crumbling concrete platform overlooking a former factory complex, now slated for luxury apartments. He's tracing faded murals on the walls – remnants of his past and the community that once thrived there; he remembers painting them with friends, fueled by cheap beer and a sense of rebellious belonging.
historia.estribillo: The chorus expresses a longing for a Buenos Aires that never truly existed – a time of gritty authenticity, shared struggle, and artistic freedom, now lost to progress and commercialization; it's a yearning for a feeling of belonging rooted in a collective past, laced with the bittersweet taste of addiction to that memory.
historia.verso2: The narrator is approached by a developer who recognizes his artwork and offers him a commission to create a 'heritage mural' for the new apartment complex.  He initially resists, feeling it's a betrayal of his ideals, but the promise of money and a renewed sense of purpose (however hollow) lures him in.
historia.puente: While painting the mural, the narrator notices a young girl sketching nearby, mirroring his own youthful passion. He realizes the 'ghosts' he's chasing aren't just about the past, but about the potential for creation and connection that exists *now*, and that clinging solely to nostalgia prevents him from shaping a new future.
